purpose: Rilonacept is used to treat recurrent pericarditis, which is a painful inflammation of the sac surrounding your heart that keeps coming back. It is also used for certain rare inherited conditions called Cryopyrin-Associated Periodic Syndromes (CAPS) in adults and children. It helps reduce pain, swelling, and other symptoms caused by these conditions.
how_it_works: Your body produces a protein called interleukin-1 (IL-1) that can trigger inflammation. In some conditions, your body makes too much of this protein, causing painful and repeated inflammation. Rilonacept works like a trap — it grabs onto IL-1 before it can cause trouble, blocking the signal that starts inflammation and helping your body calm down.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include redness, swelling, bruising, or pain at the injection site. You may also notice an increased chance of getting infections like colds or respiratory infections. Some people experience headache or mild stomach upset.
warnings: Because this medication lowers your immune system's ability to fight infections, you are at a higher risk for serious infections, including tuberculosis (TB). Tell your doctor right away if you develop fever, chills, cough, or feel very ill. Do not get live vaccines while taking this medication. Let your doctor know about all other medications and health conditions, especially if you have a history of repeated infections.
typical_dosing: For adults, rilonacept is given as a shot (injection) under the skin, usually once a week. Your doctor or nurse will teach you how to give the injection at home. The starting dose may be higher at first, and then reduced to a regular weekly maintenance dose. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions for your dose.
